title: Integrate incident-derived rollback, observability, and rollout constraints into Serving PRD
creator: Nadia Patel
description: Purpose: Incorporate concrete, incident-driven requirements from the 2025-01 KV cache outage postmortem into the Serving PRD so rollout, rollback, and observability behaviors are unambiguous and testable. Background: The postmortem identified three gaps: (1) insufficient automated rollback thresholds and lack of canary acceptance tests tied to real error signals, (2) incomplete runtime tracing and aggregated SLO signals across model variants, and (3) unclear owner/responsibility split between Console and Runtime for emergency rollbacks. This ticket updates the PRD to capture new requirements, scope boundaries, and acceptance criteria so engineering can implement deterministic fallbacks and guarded rollouts without UI/Console blockers. Documentation: Updated PRD, runbooks, and one-pager for on-call within release notes before release cut.
acceptance_criteria: Automated rollback: Runtime exposes a configurable policy that triggers automatic rollback to the previous model variant when sustained request-error-rate >= 2.0% for 90s OR tail latency p99 degradation > 50% above baseline for 60s.
Canary acceptance test: Canary rollout must pass a synthetic traffic canary with at least 95% success and p95 latency within 1.2x baseline over a 15-minute window before broader traffic ramp.

Observable signals: New aggregated SLO dashboard with token-level error rate, p95/p99 latency, kv-cache hit ratio, and model-variant-specific error attribution available in Console within the release window.
Runbook linkage: Every rollback policy has a linked runbook and a mandatory post-rollback incident ticket template created automatically when rollback is executed.
Ownership: Runtime owns low-level enforcement and execution of rollback; Console owns policy configuration UI, visibility, and one-click manual override. Hand-off documented in PRD.

Tests: Add acceptance tests that simulate KV cache miss storm and verify fallback path (model variant with same capabilities but different cache strategy) in CI with a soft-fail flag for scheduled canary runs.
No-regression: New checks added to the model rollout pipeline that block canary promotion if trace sampling is disabled or ingestion of runtime metrics is missing for >5 minutes.
Telemetry retention: Relevant trace and metric spans for rollouts retained for 90 days under runtime-1.20 release observability policy.
Backward compatibility: Existing API clients must see no semantic changes; feature flags are provided for staged rollout of PRD behaviors.
Documentation: Updated PRD, runbooks, and one-pager for on-call within release notes before release cut.
decisions: Enforce rollback thresholds in runtime (ENG) rather than only in Console to guarantee action even if Console is degraded.
Use synthetic canary traffic derived from representative prompt sets from the postmortem instead of generic health checks.
Defer advanced UI for visual policy composition to a follow-up (scope reduction): initial Console UI will be a structured form with JSON export/import.
Adopt a single source of truth for rollout state in runtime's control plane to avoid state drift between regions.
Telemetry budget: prioritize p95/p99 latency and kv-cache hit ratio metrics; span-level traces for request attribution added for canaries.
Security review: scoped changes do not introduce new data exfiltration paths; will be marked for light security audit only.
notes: Trade-offs: Automating rollback reduces manual toil and MTTR but risks unnecessary rollbacks for transient spikes; thresholds chosen to bias toward stability based on postmortem frequency analysis.
Scope: This PRD update does not include a fully interactive rollout visualizer; that work will be a separate PM ticket after runtime-1.20.
Implementation owner matrix: Runtime infra (ENG-2893) = enforcement & execution; Observability team (ENG-3012) = dashboards & retention; Console PM = config UI + docs.
Fallback mapping: When kv-cache degradation is detected, runtime will prefer fallback model variants that are quantization-compatible to avoid tokenization/regeneration differences.
Acceptance test constraints: CI can run a reduced canary simulation nightly; full synthetic canary runs must be scheduled in staging prior to prod promotion.
Risk: Synthetic canaries must mirror real user distributions; we will validate canary prompt corpus against sampled production prompts in the next cycle.

Budget/estimates: PM estimate implies staged implementation across 3 sprints; initial runtime enforcement + one CLI policy tool in sprint 1, observability dashboards sprint 2, Console UI minimal form sprint 3.
Coordination: Schedule weekly syncs with Runtime, Observability, and On-Call leads until rollout is complete.
